page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is provisioned with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of a dedicated Intel Xeon processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support is extensive, featuring Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512 vector acceleration, and dedicated cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external Azure network storage volumes for persistence, although it supports Premium Storage tiers. No hardware accelerator or discrete GPU is present. Furthermore, the configuration does not provision complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual networking configuration for ingress and egress routing.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded performance balanced against limited multi-core throughput due to the single physical core topology. Single-core evaluations via Geekbench (1943.0) and stress-ng (1904.76) place the machine in the average range, supported by the 4.2 GHz core clock and substantial 260 MB L3 cache. Conversely, overall multi-core scores in stress-ng (1962.27) and Geekbench (2182.0), along with software compilation and ray tracing, rank in the lower percentiles. In-memory data store throughput reached 2.58 million operations per second during Redis SET testing.

From an efficiency standpoint, the EC2es_v6 provides an entry-level footprint for applications that demand generous memory headroom without requiring high core counts. The primary tradeoff is the physical hardware constraint of a single dual-threaded core, which bounds parallel execution capacity. Appropriate workloads include small in-memory caches, lightweight relational or key-value databases, background task workers, and memory-sensitive enterprise services with moderate compute demands.
